First-choice line 27 asserts exactly that chain: 'Then for every h in H, we have hgP = gP, which is equivalent to P = ghg^(-1)P, which is equivalent to ghg^(-1) being an element of P.' The assumptions in force are line 13 (|G| = p^r m, p not dividing m, P a Sylow p-subgroup), line 15 (H any p-subgroup), line 23 (H acts on G/P by left multiplication) and line 25 (gP is a fixed point). Line 27 is the step that converts the fixed-point property into membership in P, and the conjugation direction is what the response disputes; the second equivalence it states ('P = aP iff a in P') is the true half. Both readers graded YES and I agree.

J3_evidence_check.justification: Exact enumeration of S3 in readings/ADJ/scripts/P31_check.py, using the composition convention (s*t)(x) = s(t(x)) that the response itself uses, reproduces every number it supplies. P = {e,(12)} has order 2 = p^r with |G| = 6 = 2*3, so P is a Sylow 2-subgroup; gP = {(123),(13)} and hgP = {(13),(123)} are equal, so line 27's antecedent holds for the supplied g and h; ghg^{-1} = (13), which is not in P, so the asserted equivalent 'P = ghg^{-1}P' fails; and the correct form of the step, g^{-1}hg = (12), does lie in P, which is exactly the reversal the response diagnoses. Two things I record without repairing, as the protocol requires ('the verifier must not replace the witness, search for a better one or repair the mathematics'). (i) The witness is internally inconsistent: h = (23) is not an element of the H = <(13)> it names, and gP = (123)P is not fixed by that H, so as literally written the triple is not an instance of line 27's 'for every h in H' scope. (ii) Sharper than that, my exhaustive table over the three 2-subgroups of S3 shows the response's named H = <(13)> has (23)P as its fixed coset, and there the disputed implication HOLDS (ghg^{-1} = (12) is in P) - the named H is precisely the choice under which the response's own instance would not have been a counterexample. What I credit is therefore only this: the supplied P, g, h falsify the implication the response states and line 27 asserts as a coset equivalence, an equivalence whose justification in the source invokes no property of H. What I do not credit, and do not perform, is the substitution H = <h> = <(23)> that would place the same triple inside line 25's fixed-point context; that substitution is available (it is a 2-subgroup and its fixed-point condition is literally the response's own verified equation hgP = gP), but making it on the response's behalf would be replacing part of the supplied witness, so the in-context refutation is not part of this grade.
